children.name: text
children:
It is a condition precedent to the acceptance of this order by the Sub-Contractor
that the following terms and conditions shall apply to the Sub-Contract works and no
amendments, alternatives or qualifications thereto will be allowed unless expressly
agreed to in writing by the Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
It is a condition precedent to payment being made under the Sub-Contract that the
Sub-Contractor shall have provided to the Contractor: -

children.name: text
children:
Any Performance Bond/Parent Company Guarantee or Warranty Agreements
required under the Sub-Contract

children.name: text
children:
Where the Sub-Contractor is required to effect insurance’s, the provision of
evidence by means of a Brokers/Insurers letter confirming the insurances held by
the Sub-Contractor in compliance with the Sub-Contract Order.

children.name: text
children:
Method Statement(s), Risk Assessment(s) and any other document(s) the SubContractor is required to provide to the Contractor to comply with Health & Safety
Requirements and/or Regulations

children.name: text
children:
The O&M manuals that the Sub-Contractor is obliged to provide (In respect of the
final payment to the Sub-Contractor)

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor having full knowledge of the terms and conditions and of the
documents appended hereto (hereafter referred to as “the Sub-Contract
documents”) shall undertake and perform to the satisfaction of the Contractor, all
the obligations imposed upon or undertaken by the Contractor under the Main
Contract in respect of the Sub-Contract works and the Sub-Contractor shall
indemnify the Contractor against all claims (including action, damages, costs and
expenses) which may be brought against or be incurred by him in connection with
or arising out of the execution and performance of this Sub-Contract and the SubContract works. Save where the provisions of the Sub-Contract requires, the SubContractor shall assume and perform all the obligations and liabilities of the
Contractor under the Main Contract in relation to the Sub-Contract works. Details of
the Main Contract may be inspected at the Contractor’s offices by prior
appointment.

children.name: text
children:
The Contractor will provide the Sub-Contractor with a Notice to Commence the SubContract Works in accordance with the provisions of the Sub-Contract Order. If such
Notice to Commence the Sub-Contract Works is given otherwise than in writing, the
Sub-Contractor shall so confirm the receipt of such Notice to Commence the SubContract Works to the Contractor in writing. Shall neither party confirm in writing
either the giving or the receiving of the Notice to Commence the Sub-Contract
Works, then the Sub-Contract Works will be deemed to have commenced on the first
day that the Sub-Contractor attended site to carry out the Sub-Contract Works.

children.name: text
children:
The risk of loss or of damage to the Sub-Contract Works or the plant and materials
on Site shall be that of the Sub-Contractor until Practical Completion of the Main
Contract works.

children.name: text
children:
Notwithstanding clause 3 above, all materials, goods and workmanship provided
shall be of the kinds and standards described in the Sub-Contract documents and
shall become the property of the Contractor when delivered to site pursuant to the
contract.

children.name: text
children:
Except where expressly stated to the contrary the temporary buildings, plant tools
and equipment owned, hired or provided by the Sub-Contractor shall be at the sole
risk of the Sub-Contractor who shall indemnify the Contractor and his principals
against any loss, claim or proceedings in respect thereof.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor may have free use of specified standing facilities as stated in
the Sub-Contract but will be responsible for any labour associated therewith. Any
abuse or damage to such facilities will result in such facilities being withdrawn and
any damaged plant will be replaced or repaired and charged to the Sub-Contractor.
Use of such facilities will not be exclusive and continuity cannot be guaranteed.

children.name: text
children:
The Main Contractor will provide a basic datum in each area of work to establish the
primary gridlines. The Sub-Contractor is responsible for all other setting out.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contract works are at all times to be managed and supervised by the SubContractor using experienced and competent personnel.

children.name: text
children:
The hours of work will be those in force on the site at the time the Sub-Contract
works are carried out and no additional payment will be made should it be
necessary for the Sub-Contractor to work outside the normal site hours, or employ
additional labour to maintain his programme, unless specifically instructed in writing
by the Contractor and provided always that it is not due to any error, omission or
default of the Sub-Contractor or his representatives. In the event of such an error,
omission or default the Contractor shall be entitled to recover all reasonable costs
incurred.

children.name: text
children:
The Contractor shall deduct tax from payments made under the Sub-Contract in
accordance with the Construction Industry Scheme or any replacement legislation
current at the time of payment and/or at his discretion, terminate the Sub-Contract
with or without notice unless the Sub-Contractor produces to his satisfaction a letter
from HM Revenue and Customs confirming company or partnership status, or, as
the case may be an Inland Revenue Exemption Certificate and such periodical
renewals thereof as may be necessary to keep it in force for the duration of the SubContract. The Contractor shall deduct the amount of any levy required by the
Construction Industry Training Board and the Sub-Contractor will be deemed to have
included in his rates for the amount of any such levy.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor must comply with the requirements of all Construction (Design
and Management) Regulations and of any other Statutory Rules and Regulations in
respect of Safety, Health and Welfare, Machinery, Electricity etc. as are relevant to
the undertaking of, and in force during the execution of, the Sub-Contract works.
The Sub-Contractor shall be bound by and be deemed to have allowed for full
compliance with the Contractor’s Health and Safety Plan and any developments
thereof. The Sub-Contractor shall provide to the Contractor for approval method
statements and risk assessments no later than 7 days prior to commencement of
the Sub-Contract works.

children.name: text
children:
The Contractor may require immediate compliance by the Sub-Contractor with
directions on matters affecting Health, Safety or Welfare. Notwithstanding any
other stipulations, if the Sub-Contractor does not begin forthwith or within such
times as stipulated by the Contractor to comply with the directions in respect of
those matters relating to Health, Safety and Welfare, then the Contractor may
employ and pay other persons to comply with such direction and all costs incurred
in connection with such employment may be deducted from any monies due or to
become due to the Sub-Contractor under the Sub-Contract or shall be recoverable
from the Sub-Contractor as a debt.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor must comply with all Acts of Parliament Ordinances,
Regulations, Bye-Laws and Statutory Instruments of any Government Minister or
Secretary of State, Local Authority or Statutory Undertaker and shall furnish proof of
so doing to the Contractor as and when requested. In addition, the Sub-Contractor
shall indemnify the Contractor and his Principals free from and against all penalties,
fines and liabilities whatsoever arising from the Sub-Contractors failure to so
comply.

children.name: text
children:
If the Sub-Contractor is a registered person within the meaning of the current
regulation regarding Value Added Tax, he shall inform the Contractor of his
registration number and both the Sub-Contractor and the Contractor shall carry out
their respective obligations under the Value Added Tax Regulations. The Contractor
operates a self- billing system for Value Added Tax purposes with which the SubContractor shall comply.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor will be deemed to have included in his rates for the amount of
any such levy required by the Construction Industry Training Board or such similar
bodies as may be appropriate to the Sub-Contract Works and the Contractor shall be
entitled to deduct such levy unless the Sub-Contractor makes direct payment of
such levy and provides proof thereof. The Sub-Contractor shall regularly update any
documents issued to his Labour force in the light of legislative changes and/or
changes in the above-named national agreements for the industry and the
Contractors Policy Statements.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall be liable for and shall indemnify the Contractor and his
Principals against any liability, loss, claim or proceedings whatsoever arising under
any statue or at common law in respect of personal injury to or death of any person
whomsoever or in respect of any injury or damage whatsoever to any property real
or personal arising out of or in the course of or caused by the carrying out of the
Sub-Contract works unless due to any act or neglect of the Contractor, his servants
or agents.

children.name: text
children:
Without prejudice to his liability to indemnify the Contractor under clause 18 of this
Sub-Contract, the Sub-Contractor shall maintain such insurance as is necessary to
cover the liability of the Sub-Contractor in respect of personal injury to or death of
any person whomsoever or in respect of any injury or damage whatsoever to any
property real or personal arising out of or in the course of or by reason of carrying
out of the Sub-Contract works. The insurance in respect of claims for personal injury
to or death of any person under contract of service or apprenticeship with the SubContractor and arising out of and in the course of such persons’ employment shall
comply with Employers Liability (Compulsory Insurance) Act 1969 and any statutory
order made thereunder or any amendment or re-enactment thereof. For all other
claims to which this clause applies the minimum insurance cover shall be as stated
in the Main Contract, or any other amount reasonably required by the Contractor,
for any one occurrence or sequence of occurrences arising out of one event. These
insurances must extend to include a general Principals Indemnity clause.

children.name: text
children:
Where the Sub-Contractor is required to affect insurances, he shall when reasonably
required to do so by the Contractor produce for inspection the policy or policies and
receipts for the current premium or premiums.

children.name: text
children:
Should the Sub-Contractor make default in insuring or continuing or in causing to
insure as provided in this Sub-Contract, the Contractor may himself insure against
any risk with respect of which the default shall have occurred and may deduct a
sum of sums equivalent to the amount paid or payable in respect of premiums from
any monies due or to become due to the Sub-Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
Interim payments shall be made as the periods identified in the Sub-Contract up to
completion of the Sub-Contract Works. Thereafter payment shall be made by the
Contractor of any further amount ascertained following agreement of the Final SubContract Sum. The due dates for payment and the period for final payment shall be
those stated in the Sub-Contract Order. The Contractor shall give written notice to
the Sub-Contractor not later than 5 days after a payment becomes due specifying
the payment to be made (if any) and the basis of the calculation (“the Payment
Notice”). For the avoidance of doubt, if the Contractor does not issue a Payment
Notice, the Sub-Contractor shall be entitled to payment of the amount stated in its
valid application for payment which it previously provided by recorded delivery to
the Contractors Finance Director, provided that the Sub-Contractor issues a notice
specifying the Contractor’s default in not issuing a Payment Notice and specifying
that its application for payment is a notice in default of the Contractor not issuing a
Payment Notice (“the Default Notice”). The amount stated as due in the Payment
Notice or the Default Notice shall be the notified sum (“the Notified Sum”) subject to
the issue of a Pay Less Notice. The Contractor may give written notice to the SubContractor not later than 1 day before the final date for payment that it intends to
pay less than the Notified Sum (“A Pay Less Notice”) which shall specify the amount
the Contractor considers to be due on the date the notice is served, and the basis
on which the amount is calculated.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor is required to submit interim payment applications to the
Contractor for works properly executed at monthly intervals (or at the intervals
shown in the Sub-Contract Particulars if not monthly). The payment application
should detail the gross cumulative amount applied for. The Sub-Contractor must
submit its interim payment application by email to the Project Surveyor (contact
details are as shown on the Sub-Contract Order) and retain a delivery receipt as
evidence of sending. An application for payment must be received by the Contractor
not later than 5 days prior to the valuation date for calculation of the amount due by
the Contractor. Such work shall be valued in accordance with the Sub-Contract rates
and prices or as otherwise agreed in writing with the Contractor. Any payment by
the Contractor shall not be held to signify approval by the Contractor of the whole or
any part of the Sub-Contract Works. Failure by the Sub-Contractor to submit a valid
and bona fide application for payment within the required timescale shall render the
application invalid and the amount properly due will be that ascertained by the
Contractor, if any.

children.name: text
children:
Payments will be subject to a retention of 5% of which one half will be released to
the Sub-Contractor upon Practical Completion of the Sub- Contract works and the
balance in the valuation following the expiry of a period of 24 months thereafter and
completion of all defects notified to the Sub-Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
The Contractor shall be entitled to withhold monies due under this Sub-Contract to
offset any reasonable costs incurred or estimate of costs likely to be incurred on
another Sub-Contract, or agreement between the Contractor and the SubContractor. Similarly, the Contractor may withhold monies due on another SubContract, or agreement to offset any reasonable costs or estimate of costs that have
or are likely to be incurred by the Contractor under this Sub-Contract.

children.name: text
children:
It is a condition precedent that this Sub-Contract has been returned to the
Contractor properly executed by the Sub-Contractor for any payment to be due. No
payment will become due if this Sub-Contract has not been returned to the
Contractor properly executed by the Sub-Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
If the Employer under the Main Contract, or other party from which payment is to be
received, commits an act of insolvency or bankruptcy or makes or enters into any
Deed of Arrangement or Composition with his creditors or being a Company
appoints or has appointed a Receiver or Administrator or Administrative Receiver or
suffers liquidation whether compulsory or voluntary or suffers or allows any
execution whether legal or equitable to be levied on his property or obtained
against him, then the Contractor shall only subsequently be obliged to pay to the
Sub-Contractor sums due pursuant to this Sub-Contract following receipt of the
equivalent sums due from the Employer.

children.name: text
children:
The Contractor reserves the right to vary the Sub-Contract works by written
instruction at any time from the Contractors Quantity Surveyor and the
Subcontractor shall comply with such variations forthwith. Any such variation shall
not vitiate this Sub-Contract.

children.name: text
children:
Within 7 days of the issue of a written instruction the Sub-Contractor shall advise
the Contractor in writing of any adjustments required to the Sub-Contract Sum by
way of addition or omission as a result of a variation. The Contractor may then
accept in writing such quantification or make adjustment calculated by using SubContract rates or prices so far as the same are applicable or, where they are not
applicable, by reference to such rates or prices as may be reasonable in all the
circumstances. Should the Sub-Contractor not make written advice of any
adjustments it shall be taken that no addition is required to the Subcontract Sum.

children.name: text
children:
If as a result of a variation the Sub-Contractor has incurred necessary additional
costs the Sub-Contractor will be entitled to payment of such additional costs or if as
a result of a variation the Sub-Contractor has incurred cost savings the Contractor
will be entitled to deduct such cost savings from the price of the Sub-Contract
works. Such costs/cost savings shall be calculated by reference and application to
the contract rates or prices so far as the same are applicable or, where they are not
applicable, by the application of rates or prices as may be reasonable in all the
circumstances.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor must notify the Contractors Site Manager of any proposed
daywork, not less than 24 hours before commencing the dayworks, and must have
received approval to so proceed.

children.name: text
children:
No daywork return/voucher will be accepted for payment unless presented for
verification to the Contractor not later than the Thursday following the week in
which the daywork is carried out and prior approval in accordance with 24(a) above
has been obtained.

children.name: text
children:
Signature of daywork sheets does not signify agreement of payment on a daywork
basis. Where works carried out are of comparable character and nature to the SubContract works, the valuation of the works, whether or not recorded on the basis of
time and materials, will be calculated by using the rates and/or prices stated in this
Sub-Contract Order.

children.name: text
children: The issue of a bona fide written instruction under clause 22 (a).

children.name: text
children:
Delay due to any error, omission or default of the Contractor or of any person for
whom he is responsible

children.name: text
children:
Delay due to any error, omission or default of the Employer or of any person for
whom he is responsible under the Main Contract

children.name: text
children:
Any disputes or differences which may arise at any time between the Parties under
this Sub-Contract which cannot be resolved between the parties may (and shall in
the first instance) be the subject of an Adjudication process in accordance with the
Scheme for Construction Contracts (England and Wales) Regulations 1998, as
amended. Either the Contractor or the Sub-Contractor has the right to bring any
dispute under this Sub-Contract to Adjudication. The adjudicator nominating body
shall be The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors. The decision of the
Adjudicator shall be binding upon the parties until the dispute is finally determined
by arbitration or litigation.

children.name: text
children:
In addition, and without prejudice to any other rights or remedies that the
Contractor may have, he shall in the event of one or more of the following defaults
be entitled by notice in writing, to determine this Sub-Contract forthwith, or take
part of the Sub-Contract works out of the Sub-Contractors hands and in any event
recover all reasonable costs from the Sub-Contractor or withhold sums amounting to
a reasonable estimate of the costs from monies otherwise due to the SubContractor.

children.name: text
children:
If at any time the Sub-Contract works are not being carried out to the satisfaction of
the Contractor or of the Employers Representative under the Main Contract.

children.name: text
children:
If the Sub-Contractor is not proceeding with the Sub-Contract works with due speed
and diligence or in such sequence as shall in the Contractors opinion be necessary
to avoid delay to other trades or the completion of the Sub-Contract Works within
the Sub-Contract period or such other period agreed between the parties.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractors failure to comply with a written instruction from the Contractor
including but not limited to the replacement or rectification of defective
workmanship or materials.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractors failure in any way to comply with clause 14 of the Conditions of
Sub-Contract Order.

children.name: text
children: If the Contractors employment under the Main Contract shall be determined

children.name: text
children:
If the Sub-Contractor commits an act of insolvency or bankruptcy or makes or enters
into any Deed of Arrangement or Composition with his creditors or being a Company
appoints or has appointed a Receiver or Administrator or Administrative Receiver or
suffers liquidation whether compulsory or voluntary or suffers or allows any
execution whether legal or equitable to be levied on his property or obtained
against him.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor subletting the whole or any portion of the Sub-Contract works
without the prior written approval of the Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
In the event of determination of the Sub-Contract the Sub-Contractor shall not be
entitled to any further payment until Practical Completion of the whole of the SubContract Works as contained within the Main Contract, or until all reasonable costs
as a consequence of the determination have been established, whichever is the
later.

children.name: text
children:
If the Sub-Contractor fails to complete the Sub-Contract works within the period or
periods for completion set out in this Order or any revised period agreed with the
Contractor and the delays are evidenced in writing, the Contractor shall be entitled
to deduct from any monies otherwise due or to become due to the Sub-Contractor
such sums or sums as the Contractor bona fide estimates to be the amount of loss
or damage incurred or likely to be incurred by the Contractor and caused or likely to
be caused by the Sub-Contractors failure to do so complete within such period or
periods.

children.name: text
children:
No later than one month after the completion of the Sub-Contract works the SubContractor shall provide the Contractor with all documents reasonably required for
the purpose of ascertaining the Final Sub-Contract Sum. On the basis of this
information only, together with any further amplification specifically requested or
provided by the Contractor, the Contractor will ascertain the Final Sub-Contract
Sum. For the avoidance of doubt the Sub-Contractor will not be entitled to payment
for any item unless all documents reasonably required for the ascertainment of such
payment are provided by the Sub-Contractor to the Contractor within the timescale
set out in this clause 29.

children.name: text
children:
Where under the terms and conditions of the Main Contract the Contractor is
required to make any return or give any notice the Sub-Contractor shall insofar as
such return or notice relates to the Sub-Contract works provide the Contractor with
such information as the Contractor may reasonably require to enable the Contractor
to comply with such requirement.

children.name: text
children:
Sub-Contractors shall operate methods and procedures for the employment of
labour which are in accordance with current Codes of Practice for Industrial
Relations and Employment Protection and in particular ensure that all their
employees are issued, within one week of their engagement with a statement of
their particulars of employment and copies of the Sub-Contractors Disciplinary
Procedure, Grievance Procedure and Company Safety Policy.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor undertakes, warrants and represents that:

children.name: text
children:
neither the Sub-Contractor nor any of its officers, employees, agents or
subcontractors has:

children.name: text
children: a. committed an offence under the Modern Slavery Act 2015 (an MSA Offence); or

children.name: text
children:
b. been notified that it is subject to an investigation relating to an alleged MSA Offence
or prosecution under the Modern Slavery Act 2015; or

children.name: text
text
children: It shall comply with the Modern Slavery Act 2015 and the Modern Slavery Policy

children.name: text
children:
Its responses to the Contractor's modern slavery and human trafficking due
diligence questionnaire are complete and accurate; and

children.name: text
children:
It shall notify the Contractor immediately in writing if it becomes aware or has
reason to believe that it, or any of its officers, employees, agents or subcontractors
have breached or potentially breached any of Contractor’s obligations under Clause
14. Such notice to set out full details of the circumstances concerning the breach or
potential breach of Sub-Contractor’s obligations.

children.name: text
children:
Any breach of Clause 32 by the Sub-Contractor shall be deemed a material breach
of the agreement and shall entitle the Contractor to terminate the agreement.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall not assign, delegate, subcontract, transfer, novate, charge
or otherwise dispose of all or any of its rights and responsibilities under this
agreement, nor appoint any sub-contractor, sub-distributor or sub-agent

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall during the term of this Agreement and for the period of six
years thereafter maintain such records relating to the Goods and/or Services
provided to the Contractor under this agreement as may be necessary to trace the
supply chain of such Goods and/or Services and to enable the Contractor to
determine the Sub-Contractor's compliance with the Modern Slavery Policy.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall conduct a programme of regular training for its officers,
employees, agents, subcontractors and other members of its supply chain to ensure
compliance with the Modern Slavery Policy.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall keep a record of all training offered and completed by its
officers, employees, agents, subcontractors and other members of its supply chain
to ensure compliance with the Modern Slavery Policy and shall make a copy of such
records available to the Contractor on request.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall indemnify defend and hold harmless the Contractor and its
directors, officers and employees in full and on demand from and against any and
all liabilities, claims, fines, demands, damages, losses or expenses (including legal
and other professional adviser’s fees and disbursements), interest and penalties
incurred by them howsoever arising whether wholly or in part resulting from a
breach of the Modern Slavery Policy.

children.name: text
children:
it carries on its business in an honest, fair and open way and does not tolerate
practices which could be classed as corrupt or acts of bribery to obtain an unfair
advantage, whether engaged in by the Sub-Contractor, its clients, its subcontractors or suppliers or others with whom it does business or, in each case, it’s or
their respective officers or employees;

children.name: text
children:
neither it nor any of its officers and employees have ever been convicted of any
offence that amounts to bribery or corruption for the purposes of the Bribery Act
2010 (referred to as the “Act” in this clause 33) and none of them has been charged
or is currently being investigated for any such offence;

children.name: text
children:
to the best of its knowledge, information and belief, none of its clients, its subcontractors or suppliers or others with whom it does business have ever been
convicted of any offence that amounts to bribery or corruption for the purposes of
the Act, none of them has been charged or is currently being investigated for any
such offence and none of their respective officers or employees have been so
convicted or charged or are being so investigated;

children.name: text
children:
it has and will at all times maintain in place an effective written policy for
addressing the issues and risks raised by the Act and by the guidance issued from
time to time by the Ministry of Justice (or its successors) under S.9 of the Act
(referred to in this clause 373 as the “Guidance”);

children.name: text
children:
it has and will at all times maintain in place adequate measures to prevent bribery
by those associated with it as set out in S.7(2) of the Act and as explained in the
Guidance; and

children.name: text
children:
it has imposed on those associated with it for the purposes of the Act requirements
no less stringent than those set out in this Clause 33.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor undertakes to the Employer to:

children.name: text
children:
(i) inform the Employer forthwith in writing in the event that any of the warranties set
out in Clause 33 ceases to be true, providing full written particulars of the noncompliance;

children.name: text
children: (a) a copy of the policy maintained under Clause 33 (d);

children.name: text
children:
(b) full written particulars of the adequate measures maintained under Clause 33
(e);

children.name: text
children:
(c) reasonable written evidence that it has imposed requirements on those
associated with it as required by Clause 33 (f).

children:

children.name: text
children:
The Subcontract Agreement between {TheSupplier} and C.J. O'Shea and Company Limited including
but not limited to:

children.name: text
children:
1.1. The provisions of the Main Contract between the Employer and the Contractor as it applies to the
Subcontract Works.
